Agreed next steps: exchange artifacts, run baseline hosted benchmarks, then run Dedicated/Private pilot if baselines meet cost/latency thresholds.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Connor Wu (Redwood CSM) ; Dr. Alan Cho (PrimeCare Head of AI), Samantha Ruiz (VP Product), Devon Park (SRE), Kira Gomez (Clinical PM)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um quick agenda — finalize the quality eval plan and confirm the POC scope.
00:21 Dr. Alan Cho: Yep, thanks Jordan. We want to make sure the model doesn't hallucinate clinical advice, format of outputs must match our EHR ingestion pipeline, and latency needs to be under 800ms p95 for triage flows.
00:40 Maya Patel: Got it, we'll build the benchmark matrix around those — define golden prompts, regression set, hallucination checks, and also measure token-level cost.
00:55 Samantha Ruiz: One note, for success criteria product needs: 1) accuracy on our golden set >= 90% pass, 2) hallucination less than 2% on clinical facts, 3) p95 latency < 800ms on our expected concurrency of 20 qps.
01:15 Jordan Lee: Thanks Sam. Quick qual question — are those golden prompts patient anonymized? you mentioned redacted logs earlier.
01:26 Dr. Alan Cho: Yes we'll send redacted examples, but we also have synthetic prompts that mimic the distribution. we'll share 10 canonical golden prompts and 50 regression examples.
01:40 Maya Patel: That works. For the benchmark we'll need sequence length distribution, average tokens per request, and concurrency patterns. Devon can you confirm SRE numbers?
01:52 Devon Park: Typical triage requests are short — 80 to 180 tokens; discharge summaries are long — up to 1,200 tokens but those are low qps. We'll aim to capture two profiles: triage (fast, high qps) and summarization (long, low qps).
02:12 Jordan Lee: Excellent — so benchmark matrix will have at least: short/triage profile at 20 qps target and long/summarization profile at 1-2 qps. We'll run with hosted baseline first then Dedicated if needed.
02:30 Samantha Ruiz: And dataset sensitivity — we require SOC 2 controls and that logs are encrypted at rest. Also curious about KMS/HSM options if we go Private.
02:45 Maya Patel: Noted. Private supports KMS integration; we will include security docs in the package. Jordan will share the SOC 2 / security pack.
03:05 Jordan Lee: On scoring approach: proposed hybrid scoring. Automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE is not great for clinical; we'll use a mix: exact answer matching for structured fields, semantic similarity + human review for open text, and hallucination flags).
03:28 Dr. Alan Cho: How are you defining hallucination?
03:32 Maya Patel: We'll treat hallucination as any generated statement asserting a clinical fact or medication not present in the source or contradicted by the source. We'll include heuristics plus a small classifier to detect likely hallucinations; then random sample human review to confirm.
03:50 Samantha Ruiz: For structured outputs we need strict format checks — JSON schema enforcement; if the model returns malformed JSON it's a fail.
04:05 Maya Patel: Agreed. We'll include format validation in pipeline and calculate a format-failure rate.
04:20 Jordan Lee: For golden prompts we want a set that covers the main user journeys: triage question, med reconciliation, discharge summary extraction, and follow-up recommendation. Dr. Cho will provide those 10.
04:37 Dr. Alan Cho: Yep, I'll send them.
04:45 Jordan Lee: On regression tests: we'll seed 50 examples with known expected outputs. Regression pass threshold proposed at 90% exact/structure pass for structured items and 85% for semantic QA.
05:02 Samantha Ruiz: Are those thresholds negotiable?
05:06 Jordan Lee: They're starting points. If initial runs fall short we'll tune prompts, quantization profiles, or consider Dedicated/Private deployment for determinism.
05:19 Maya Patel: Important to note — quantization can change output fidelity. For clinical tasks we might recommend fp16 or carefully validated quant configs. We'll record any quality regressions with quant.
05:36 Devon Park: Latency and cost tradeoffs matter — we have budget constraints. What cost-per-1k tokens might look like?
05:44 Jordan Lee: We'll include approximate cost estimates in the spreadsheet for hosted vs dedicated. Baseline hosted will give per-token unit cost; Dedicated gives better predictability at higher commits.
06:00 Connor Wu: Also we'll include a 'regression alert' mechanism in Redwood Console so if deployed model drifts beyond thresholds we trigger rollback.
06:12 Samantha Ruiz: Good, automation is key.
06:18 Jordan Lee: Timing — propose timeline: artifacts exchange by Apr 6, baseline hosted benchmark week of Apr 13, initial quality report by Apr 17, decision point for Dedicated/Private by Apr 24. Does that align?
06:34 Dr. Alan Cho: Yes sounds reasonable.
06:37 Samantha Ruiz: One more — for hallucination detection, can Redwood provide example tooling or a rubric we can use for human reviewers?
06:44 Maya Patel: Yes we'll share a rubric and an evaluation sheet; it's the same template we used for other health customers (we will anonymize).
06:52 Jordan Lee: We'll share the internal quality eval spreadsheet and an example results dashboard link (note: sample link Redwood will attach in follow-up).
07:03 Kira Gomez: For format validation, can you also include sample schema for our EHR ingestion?
07:08 Jordan Lee: Please send the schema, Kira, we'll add checks.
07:12 Kira Gomez: Will do.
07:15 Dr. Alan Cho: On competitor consideration — we evaluated Anthropic for safety but they were expensive for our throughput; we also tried a small test with OpenAI but needed private hosting.
07:31 Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll include comparative notes but focus on objective metrics.
07:38 Maya Patel: Benchmark details I'll prepare: workloads, sequence length distribution, concurrency, latency p50/p95, token cost, hallucination rate, format-failure rate, and human-verified accuracy.
07:53 Devon Park: For the benchmark runner, will Redwood run it in our VPC or do we provide runner infra?
07:58 Jordan Lee: For baseline hosted we'll run from Redwood side to measure hosted performance. For Private/Dedicated we can either run within your VPC with permission or provide a runner that mimics your network conditions; we'll coordinate.
08:15 Samantha Ruiz: OK. Also need to understand what logs Redwood collects during POC and retention.
08:22 Connor Wu: We'll share our default retention policy and can restrict or redact logs per agreement; we'll surface what fields are collected.
08:30 Dr. Alan Cho: We prefer minimal PII in logs; redaction is required.
08:36 Jordan Lee: We'll include a redaction checklist.
08:40 Maya Patel: Back to scoring — propose scoring sheet columns: example_id, profile, expected_output, model_output, exact_match_flag, semantic_score(0-1), hallucination_flag, format_pass_flag, reviewer_notes. Aggregates: exact_match_pct, semantic_avg, hallucination_pct, format_fail_pct.
09:05 Samantha Ruiz: That seems thorough. For semantic scoring what's the human process?
09:09 Maya Patel: Humans rate on a 0-1 scale for correctness/utility for open text; we'll average across 3 reviewers for high-sensitivity examples.
09:18 Dr. Alan Cho: Sounds good. Also can we include regression windows — e.g. if drift >5% week-over-week trigger an incident?
09:29 Jordan Lee: Yes we can configure alerts. We'll put a proposed rule in the evaluation doc.
09:35 Samantha Ruiz: On outputs used for EHR — can we make sure model outputs also carry provenance metadata? case id, model version, prompt id.
09:45 Maya Patel: Absolutely — we'll include prompt_id and model_version in the envelope.
09:51 Jordan Lee: Any more questions on the plan or success criteria?
09:54 Dr. Alan Cho: No, next steps are clear. We'll aim to send golden prompts and logs by Apr 6.
09:59 Jordan Lee: Great. We'll send the quality eval spreadsheet, security docs, and a proposed benchmark runbook by Mar 30-31.
10:10 Samantha Ruiz: Thanks team.
10:12 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

Post-call notes: some transcription artifacts — Speaker labels approximate; references to docs: "quality_eval_spreadsheet.xlsx" (shared link in follow-up), "security_pack.zip" (link), and benchmark runner notes (will be attached).
